etymologies.heading: Etymology
paragraphs: From Middle English noysom; equivalent to noy +‎ -some (short for annoy, from an(n)oien, enoien from Anglo-Norman anuier, from Old French enuier (French ennuyer), from Late Latin inodiare, from in- (intensive prefix) + odium (“hate”)).
senses: (literary) Hurtful or noxious to health; unwholesome, insalubrious.
